original_question: Study the geometric properties of the Markov spectrum.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 21: "Study geometric properties of Markov spectrum." It is introduced there as the third further open question and is explicitly said to be related to the study of minima of decomposable forms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official formulation essentially verbatim, and it correctly targets the geometric viewpoint rather than neighboring questions on sail faces, combinatorics, or statistics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
missing_details: The paper places this problem in the framework of geometric multidimensional continued fractions, not as an isolated question about the classical Markov spectrum alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
The ambient setting is real n-dimensional space with the integer lattice Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The nearby contextual definition is the sail construction of Definition 2.2; that is the geometric language in which the paper connects Markov minima to continued fractions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
The relevant objects are decomposable forms whose linear factors determine an arrangement of hyperplanes via their kernels. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
The paper’s concrete geometric bridge is that the minima of such a decomposable form occur at vertices of the corresponding sails. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The classical two-dimensional case is mentioned only as a reference point; the paper does not restate Problem 21 as only a classical n=2 question, so a stand-alone rewrite should avoid that unintended restriction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
refined_question: In the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions, study the geometric properties of the Markov spectrum arising from Markov minima of decomposable forms on R^n with respect to the lattice Z^n, using the fact that the minima of such a form are attained at vertices of the sails associated, in the sense of Definition 2.2, to the hyperplane arrangement given by the kernels of its linear factors. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Problem 21 in Section 4, not the broader statistical questions on sail distributions from Section 3.4 and not any neighboring question about face types or torus decompositions. The only nearby context that sharpens Problem 21 is the remark in Section 2.2 on Markov minima, which says that the minima of a decomposable form occur at vertices of sails associated to the hyperplanes given by the kernels of its linear factors, together with Definition 2.2, which supplies the sail formalism. Because the paper gives no narrower equivalent reformulation, the faithful refinement is to keep the original problem and add precisely this geometric context, without broadening it or restricting it to a different special case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
